name: Below the Threshold
description: A serialized neural-feed crime drama in which players inhabit rotating perspectives — a Shelf enforcer, a debt runner, and a Tier 2 social worker — across a single interconnected case involving organ-stripping rings and corponation insurance fraud. Each episode drops the viewer into a different body mid-scene, with no recap, forcing emotional continuity through sensation rather than narrative summary. The show's refusal to editorialize made it genuinely unsettling — viewers frequently reported difficulty distinguishing their own memories from the feed.
cultural_impact: Sparked the so-called 'perspective fatigue' discourse — a widespread debate about whether neural-feed empathy was genuine or a commodified simulation of solidarity.
story_hooks: A player realizes one episode's 'fictional' enforcer memory matches a real unsolved disappearance in their district.
The dissolved studio's final episode was never released — someone is selling what they claim is the master file.
A Tier 4 attorney quietly lobbying against the Vantablack suit has her own reasons for wanting the organ-ring storyline buried.
